questions.question: What type of restaurant is Jinbeh?
questions.primaryKeyword: what type of restaurant is jinbeh
questions.answer: Jinbeh is a family-owned Japanese restaurant serving hibachi (teppanyaki) and sushi in the Dallas-Fort Worth area since the Matsuda family founded Jinbeh in 1988. We operate two locations: Frisco at 2693 Preston Road near Stonebriar Centre and Toyota Stadium, and Lewisville at 2440 S Stemmons Freeway near Vista Ridge Mall. Our menu centers on tableside hibachi cooking, fresh sushi, and traditional Japanese entrées like ramen, tempura, and donburi. Jinbeh is not a chain or franchise; we are independently still family-owned and operated. We are best known for our signature mustard sauce, fried rice, and the teppanyaki performance our chefs put on at every hibachi table.
questions.expandedContent: Jinbeh has been a fixture in DFW dining for more than three decades, originally opening in Lewisville before adding the Frisco location to serve growing North Texas. While many guests come to us for the hibachi show, our sushi program is just as serious, daily fish selections, classic nigiri, sashimi, and specialty rolls developed over years of refinement. We are a full-service sit-down restaurant with hibachi tables, sushi bar seating, traditional dining tables, and a full bar featuring sake, Japanese whisky, beer, and wine. Because we are family-owned, you will often see the same chefs, servers, and managers year after year. That continuity is unusual in the restaurant industry and is one of the reasons OpenTable guests have rated us 4.6 stars in Frisco and 4.7 stars in Lewisville across more than 1,000 combined reviews.

questions.question: How long has Jinbeh been in business?
questions.primaryKeyword: how long has jinbeh been in business
questions.answer: Jinbeh has been serving the Dallas-Fort Worth area since the Matsuda family founded Jinbeh in 1988, making it one of the longest-running family-owned Japanese restaurants in North Texas. The original Lewisville location opened first, followed by Frisco. We have remained independently still family-owned and operated for more than 35 years, surviving the rise of national hibachi chains, the 2008 recession, and the 2020 pandemic. Many of our hibachi chefs and servers have been with us for over a decade. That tenure is rare in the restaurant industry and reflects our commitment to consistency, the same mustard sauce, the same fried rice, the same teppanyaki show that DFW families have loved across three generations of guests.
questions.expandedContent: When Jinbeh opened in 1988, hibachi dining was still a relatively new concept in suburban Texas. We helped introduce thousands of DFW families to tableside Japanese cooking, sushi, and sake. Today we serve guests whose parents or grandparents celebrated birthdays at our tables decades ago. Being family-owned for 35+ years means decisions are made by people who eat in the dining room, not a corporate office in another state. It also means we can move quickly, adjusting menus seasonally, sourcing fresh fish daily, and accommodating special requests without bureaucracy. Longevity in restaurants is earned one meal at a time, and we are grateful to the community that has kept us in business since the late 1980s.

The Frisco restaurant is at 2693 Preston Road, Suite 1040, in a shopping center near Stonebriar Centre and Toyota Stadium, phone (214) 619-1200. The Lewisville restaurant is at 2440 S Stemmons Freeway, Suite A, just off I-35E near Vista Ridge Mall and Castle Hills, phone (214) 488-2224. Both locations offer hibachi tables, sushi bar seating, a full bar, and ample free parking. They share the same menu and family ownership but have separate kitchens and reservation books. Both restaurants are independently staffed but share recipes, ownership, and standards. questions.question: Is Jinbeh family-owned?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh is a family-owned and independently operated Japanese restaurant, not a chain or franchise. Both Frisco and Lewisville have been family-owned and operated since the Matsuda family founded Jinbeh in 1988. Decisions about menu, hiring, sourcing, and hospitality are made by owners who are in the dining room, not by a corporate office in another state. This is a meaningful difference from national hibachi chains. Family ownership lets us keep long-tenured chefs, adjust menus seasonally, accommodate special requests, and maintain consistent quality across decades. When you celebrate a birthday or anniversary at Jinbeh, you are supporting an independent DFW small business.
questions.expandedContent: The restaurant industry chews through ownership constantly, most independent restaurants close within five years. Jinbeh has survived for more than 35 years because the family ownership has stayed invested, hands-on, and responsive to the community. Many of our servers and hibachi chefs have been with us a decade or longer; that tenure is impossible at chains where labor turnover is built into the model. Family ownership also means we can support local schools, churches, soccer teams, and charity events without asking permission from a regional manager. If you have ever donated a gift card to a school auction in Frisco or Lewisville, there is a good chance Jinbeh contributed to it.

questions.answer: No, Jinbeh is not a chain or franchise. We are a family-owned Japanese restaurant with two locations in the DFW area, Frisco and Lewisville, both owned and operated by the same family stewardship since the Matsuda family founded Jinbeh in 1988. Unlike national hibachi chains and franchise steakhouses, Jinbeh has no corporate parent company, no franchisees, and no out-of-state ownership. questions.expandedContent: The hibachi category in North Texas is dominated by chains, which makes Jinbeh's independence unusual. Chains optimize for consistency at scale, which often means frozen ingredients, centralized purchasing, and rigid menus. We optimize for the guest sitting in front of us tonight, which means fresh fish deliveries, flexibility on dietary needs, and long-tenured chefs who actually know the regulars by name. The owners live in DFW, eat at the restaurants, and is reachable when there is a problem. If you have a great experience or a bad one, the people who own Jinbeh will hear about it directly.

questions.question: What's the difference between Jinbeh Frisco and Lewisville?
questions.answer: Jinbeh Frisco and Jinbeh Lewisville share the same family ownership, menu, recipes, and standards, but they are two physically separate restaurants with a few real differences. Frisco is at 2693 Preston Road near Stonebriar Centre and Toyota Stadium and uses gas-powered hibachi grills. Lewisville is at 2440 S Stemmons Freeway near Vista Ridge Mall and uses electric hibachi grills. Frisco trends slightly busier for dinner and weekends; Lewisville is often easier for last-minute reservations. Both have full bars, sushi bars, hibachi tables, and ample parking. Pick whichever location is closer or has the time slot you need on OpenTable.
questions.expandedContent: Gas versus electric hibachi grills is a subtle but real difference. Gas grills heat faster, recover heat more quickly between proteins, and produce slightly more dramatic flame effects during the show, guests who grew up on classic Benihana-style hibachi often prefer the Frisco experience. Electric grills (Lewisville) provide a more even, consistent heat and are easier to keep at precise temperatures. Both styles produce excellent food; experienced chefs adjust their technique to the equipment. OpenTable reviews give Lewisville a slight edge (4.7 vs 4.6 stars), but both locations are well above DFW average. If you live between the two, your choice often comes down to traffic, parking, and which side of the metroplex you are on that evening.

questions.question: What is the history of Jinbeh?
questions.answer: Jinbeh opened in 1988 as a family-owned Japanese restaurant in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, originally in Lewisville. The family ownership launched the restaurant during an era when hibachi dining was still a novelty in suburban Texas and helped introduce thousands of DFW families to teppanyaki, sushi, and sake. Over the next three decades, Jinbeh expanded to a second location in Frisco at 2693 Preston Road near Stonebriar Centre. The restaurant has stayed independently owned and family-operated through every major industry shift, the rise of chain hibachi, the 2008 recession, the 2020 pandemic, without losing its identity, recipes, or core staff. Many chefs and servers have been with Jinbeh for more than a decade.
questions.expandedContent: Jinbeh's longevity is a function of consistency. The mustard sauce, the fried rice, the teppanyaki show, and the hospitality have stayed essentially the same across generations of guests. Diners who came to Jinbeh as children in the early 1990s now bring their own kids for birthdays and graduations. That continuity is rare and intentional, the family ownership has resisted franchising, corporate buyout, or aggressive expansion in favor of running two restaurants well. Today Jinbeh maintains a 4.6-star OpenTable rating in Frisco and 4.7 stars in Lewisville across more than 1,000 combined reviews, and is a recognized DFW institution for hibachi and sushi.

questions.question: What makes Jinbeh special?
questions.answer: What makes Jinbeh special is the way the staff treats every guest like family, and they've been doing it since 1988. Servers remember regulars by name and have welcomed three generations of the same families for 20, 25, even 30+ years. Birthdays get three special touchpoints: the chef giving the birthday guest the spotlight during the hibachi show, a complimentary birthday dessert, and a $25 gift card for the birthday month. Kids receive hand-folded origami cranes from a basket by the door, plus training chopsticks and a lollipop. Authentic Japanese touches, including a traditional kimono displayed at the Frisco location, set the atmosphere. Every sauce is made fresh in-house, with the signature garlic butter prepared the day before. Each location features unique specialty sushi rolls, some co-created by regular guests through the omakase experience.
questions.expandedContent: Guests say it best. One regular wrote: "I have gone here for my birthday every year since I was at least 7. I'm 24 now and celebrated my 24th there. Truly my favorite place to be." Another: "Absolutely the best #1 Japanese Hibachi in the world. I've experienced Kobe's, Japon, Benihana and Shogun, Jinbeh by far beats them all in quality, atmosphere, cleanliness, customers all nice, food is spectacular." The magic is in the details: house-made Yum Yum sauce, signature dipping sauces, and the proprietary garlic butter (prepared the day before so the flavors meld). The hibachi performance, onion volcano, knife tricks, shrimp tossing, turns every meal into a celebration. The festive atmosphere, the long-tenured staff (many chefs and servers 10+ years), and the unique specialty rolls at each location combine into something corporate chains cannot replicate. What started in Las Colinas in 1988, featured by D Magazine as early as 1990, has become a multigenerational tradition for North Texas families.

questions.question: What does the name Jinbeh mean?
questions.answer: The name Jinbeh was once a common surname among Japanese farmers and peasants during the feudal medieval ages of Japan. These hardworking people cultivated the rice paddies that fed entire villages, embodying values of humility, honesty, and dedication. When Jinbeh first opened in 1988, the founder chose the name deliberately. Coming from humble beginnings himself, he came from a poor family and built the restaurant from nothing into what it is today. The name serves as a daily reminder of where he came from and the three values that became the spiritual foundation of the business: humble, hardworking, and honest. Those same values still guide everything Jinbeh does today, in the family ownership that continues to run both locations.
questions.expandedContent: The three-word philosophy of humble, hardworking, and honest shows up across every detail of the restaurant. It is why the kitchen takes the time to make every sauce in-house, including the proprietary garlic butter that is prepared the day before so the flavors meld. It is why the head sushi chef, who has been at Jinbeh for nearly 30 years, still trains every new sushi team member personally. It is why the floor team remembers regular guests by name and welcomes back three generations of the same families. What started in a small Las Colinas space, featured by D Magazine as early as 1990, has become a multi-generational tradition. The name Jinbeh carries the weight of where the family came from and the work it took to get here.

Many first-time daters start at the bar for a sake or Japanese whisky tasting and move to a dining room table for the meal. The Frisco location is described by guests as having a stunning sushi bar, intimate hibachi tables, and warm ambiance. Happy Hour (Monday to Friday, 5:00 to 6:30 PM, $4 draft, $5 sake, $6 wine) is a popular low-pressure first-date window. For best results, reserve on OpenTable and mention it is a first date so the team can prepare.
questions.expandedContent: First-date logistics matter. Both locations have ample free parking and entry points that work for either person arriving first. Dress code is smart casual, so the date does not require dressing up. The dining room is dim enough to feel intimate but not so dark that ordering becomes awkward. The hibachi table seats 8 to 10 and is often shared with other parties, which can break the ice on a first date or work against a quieter first impression. If you want a quieter first date, request the sushi bar or a dining room table when booking. If you want a more energetic, conversation-driven date with built-in entertainment, hibachi is the move.

questions.question: What is hibachi at Jinbeh?
questions.answer: Hibachi at Jinbeh is tableside Japanese cooking on a large iron griddle (teppanyaki style), performed by a skilled chef directly in front of your group. A typical hibachi meal at Jinbeh includes onion soup, salad with ginger dressing, fried rice, grilled vegetables, and your choice of protein, chicken, shrimp, scallops, steak, filet mignon, lobster tail, or combinations. The chef performs knife tricks, builds the famous onion volcano, and cooks each protein to order on the grill. Hibachi tables seat up to 10 guests around the grill. The experience runs about 60 to 75 minutes and includes our signature mustard sauce, ginger sauce, and yum yum sauce.
questions.expandedContent: Technically, what most American restaurants call 'hibachi' is teppanyaki, cooking on a flat iron griddle. True traditional hibachi refers to a small charcoal grill. In DFW and across the US, the terms are used interchangeably for tableside Japanese griddle cooking, and that is what Jinbeh has served since 1988. Our Frisco location uses gas-powered grills and Lewisville uses electric, both producing the high, even heat needed for the show. Hibachi is a dine-in only experience because the entertainment and the food arrive together; we do not do hibachi takeout because the rice, vegetables, and proteins lose their character in a to-go container. Reservations are strongly recommended, especially for groups of six or more.

questions.question: What's the difference between hibachi and teppanyaki?
questions.answer: Technically, hibachi is a traditional Japanese charcoal grill, while teppanyaki is cooking on a flat iron griddle. In American restaurants, including Jinbeh, the word 'hibachi' is commonly used for what is technically teppanyaki: tableside cooking on a large flat griddle with a chef performing knife tricks and the onion volcano. Both terms refer to the same experience at Jinbeh's Frisco and Lewisville locations. Our chefs cook your proteins, vegetables, and fried rice on a heated iron surface right at your table. In Japan, the distinction matters more; in the US, the terms have effectively merged. When you book a 'hibachi' table at Jinbeh, you are getting teppanyaki-style cooking.
questions.expandedContent: The terminology confusion dates back to the 1960s when Benihana introduced teppanyaki to America under the name 'hibachi.' The name stuck. Today most Americans use 'hibachi' to mean any tableside Japanese griddle cooking, regardless of fuel source or equipment. Jinbeh's chefs are trained in classic teppanyaki technique: precise temperature control, choreographed knife work, and the timing required to bring rice, vegetables, and three or four proteins to a single hot plate simultaneously. Frisco's gas grills and Lewisville's electric grills both produce the high, even heat the technique requires. Whether you call it hibachi or teppanyaki, the show and the food are the same.

questions.question: How much does hibachi cost at Jinbeh?
questions.answer: Hibachi dinner entrées at Jinbeh range from approximately $25 to $50 per person depending on the protein you choose. Family-friendly options like chicken teriyaki and shrimp are on the lower end. Premium cuts like filet mignon, ribeye, NY strip, scallops, and lobster tail are at the higher end. Combination platters (steak and chicken, steak and shrimp, steak and lobster, seafood combo) and the Imperial Dinner fall between. Every hibachi entree includes Japanese onion soup, ginger-dressing salad, hibachi vegetables, fried or steamed rice, and the signature sauces. The best value is the Hibachi-for-Two lunch special: $35 for two hibachi entrees with all the courses, available Monday through Friday from 11 AM to 2 PM as a limited-time weekday offer. Jinbeh does not offer all-you-can-eat dining.
questions.expandedContent: For current pricing, call Frisco at (214) 619-1200 or Lewisville at (214) 488-2224, or view the latest menu on the website. Add-ons that can extend the total per-person cost include sashimi or sushi rolls from the sushi bar, premium sake, Japanese whisky, hand-crafted cocktails, and dessert. Happy Hour (Monday through Friday, 5:00 to 6:30 PM) offers $4 draft beer, $5 sake, and $6 wine, which can offset the cost of beverages for couples or small groups. Private dining and group reservations have different pricing structures, so for groups of 10 or more, contact the catering team for a custom quote.

questions.question: What comes with a hibachi dinner at Jinbeh?
questions.answer: A hibachi dinner at Jinbeh includes onion soup, salad with house ginger dressing, hibachi vegetables (zucchini, onion, mushroom), fried rice, and your choice of protein cooked tableside by the chef. The meal also includes our three signature dipping sauces: mustard sauce, ginger sauce, and yum yum sauce. The chef performs the meal in front of your group on the grill, including the onion volcano. White rice or noodles can be substituted for fried rice on request. Add-on options include additional shrimp, scallops, fried rice, side sushi rolls, soup upgrades, and dessert. The experience runs about 60 to 75 minutes from seating to dessert.
questions.expandedContent: Hibachi dinners are designed to feel abundant, most guests leave full and often with leftovers. The order on the grill is intentional: soup first, then salad, then vegetables, then rice, then proteins, finishing with the protein the table ordered last. This sequencing keeps everything hot and ensures your steak is not waiting under a lamp while your shrimp finishes. The mustard sauce is the most-asked-about element on the menu, it is a Jinbeh recipe with a creamy, slightly sweet, mildly spicy profile that pairs especially well with chicken and steak. Many guests order extra to take home. We are happy to send mustard sauce in to-go containers if you ask your server.

questions.question: What is Jinbeh's mustard sauce?
questions.answer: Jinbeh's mustard sauce is our signature creamy hibachi dipping sauce, served with every hibachi meal at both Frisco and Lewisville locations. The recipe combines mustard powder, sesame, cream, and a few proprietary ingredients into a smooth, slightly sweet, mildly spicy sauce that pairs especially well with chicken, steak, and shrimp. It is one of the most-asked-about menu items at Jinbeh, many DFW guests have been eating it for years and consider it the defining flavor of a Jinbeh hibachi dinner. Yes, you can request extra mustard sauce at the table, and yes, we will package it for takeout if you want to bring some home. The recipe has been the same since 1988.
questions.expandedContent: Mustard sauce gets attention because most hibachi restaurants only serve the standard 'yum yum' (white/pink) sauce and a ginger sauce. Jinbeh's mustard sauce is a third option that has become a signature of the brand. The sauce is creamy enough to coat fried rice or grilled steak without overpowering it, with just enough mustard heat to register on the palate. Pairing notes: try mustard sauce with chicken hibachi and fried rice for the classic Jinbeh combination, or with shrimp for a sharper contrast. The sauce is made fresh and contains dairy and mustard, guests with allergies to either should request alternatives. We do not currently sell mustard sauce in retail bottles, but feel free to ask for extra to take home.

Many guests come to Jinbeh just for sushi without ordering hibachi at all. Sit at the sushi bar to watch our sushi chefs work, or order sushi at any dining table. Popular options include salmon nigiri, tuna sashimi, the Jinbeh roll, rainbow roll, dragon roll, and seasonal specials. Sushi is available for lunch, dinner, and takeout (through Grubhub, Uber Eats, or direct call orders). Vegetarian sushi options include cucumber, avocado, and vegetable rolls.
questions.expandedContent: Hibachi restaurants often treat sushi as a side program, but Jinbeh has invested in sushi seriously for 35+ years. Our sushi chefs handle daily fish deliveries and prepare orders to spec, extra wasabi on the side, no avocado, gluten-free soy sauce, etc. The sushi bar is a great seat for solo diners or couples who want a quieter experience than the hibachi tables. Specialty rolls are where we have the most fun: rolls combining classic Japanese technique with Texas-friendly flavors developed over years. Sushi takeout travels well, order through Grubhub or Uber Eats, or call your location directly for pickup. Hibachi is dine-in only, but sushi is fully available to-go.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have Sushi? | Fresh Daily Sushi Bar in DFW
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh has a full sushi bar at both Frisco and Lewisville locations with daily fresh fish, nigiri, sashimi, and specialty rolls since 1988.

questions.question: What kind of fish does Jinbeh serve?
questions.answer: Jinbeh serves a rotating selection of fresh fish at our sushi bars in Frisco and Lewisville. Core selections include salmon, tuna (akami and toro when available), yellowtail (hamachi), white tuna (escolar), eel (unagi), shrimp (ebi), crab, octopus (tako), and mackerel (saba). Seasonal additions like uni, ikura, snapper, and king salmon appear when our fishmonger sources them. Fish is delivered fresh, not frozen for service. Hibachi-grilled proteins on the dinner menu include chicken, shrimp, scallops, steak, filet mignon, lobster tail, and salmon hibachi. Ask the sushi chef what looks best that day, they often have off-menu pieces from the morning's delivery.
questions.expandedContent: Sushi quality is a function of sourcing and turnover. Jinbeh has been buying from established DFW seafood suppliers for decades, which gives us first call on premium product. Tuna, salmon, and yellowtail are the daily core. Specialty fish, toro, uni, real wagyu when available, depends on what comes in that week. If you have a fish you want and we do not see it on the menu, ask; we can sometimes accommodate. We do not serve fish we are not confident in, and any unsold portion of a delivery is rotated or repurposed. For raw fish, our team follows standard sushi-grade handling protocols including proper temperature control and time-since-catch tracking.
questions.metaTitle: What Fish Does Jinbeh Serve? | Daily Fresh Sushi Selection
questions.metaDescription: Jinbeh's sushi bar serves salmon, tuna, yellowtail, eel, octopus, and seasonal fish like uni and toro. Daily fresh deliveries, never frozen for service.

questions.question: Is Jinbeh's fish fresh?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh serves fresh fish daily at both Frisco and Lewisville sushi bars. We receive deliveries from established DFW seafood suppliers most days, and our sushi chefs select cuts based on what arrives that morning. Fish is held at proper sushi-grade temperatures with strict time-since-catch tracking. We do not refreeze raw fish for service. Some specific species, most notably tuna, are flash-frozen at sea per FDA sushi-grade guidelines to neutralize parasites; this is industry standard and required for safe raw consumption. Beyond compliance, our long-tenured sushi chefs are picky about quality and will pull product that does not meet our standards. If something looks off, it does not go on a plate.
questions.expandedContent: Freshness in sushi has two dimensions: how recently the fish was caught/handled, and how it has been stored. Some species like tuna are flash-frozen on the boat, this is actually safer for raw consumption than 'fresh-never-frozen' tuna because freezing kills parasites. Other species like salmon are typically farm-raised under controlled conditions and arrive chilled. Either way, the question is whether the fish has been handled properly between the boat and your plate. Jinbeh has been sourcing sushi fish for 35+ years and has established relationships with reliable DFW seafood suppliers. If you have specific questions about a fish's provenance, ask the sushi chef, they can usually tell you where it came from.
questions.metaTitle: Is Jinbeh's Fish Fresh? | Daily Sushi Bar Sourcing in DFW
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh sources fresh fish daily from DFW seafood suppliers. Long-tenured sushi chefs, strict handling protocols, and 35+ years of sourcing experience.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have toro?
questions.answer: Toro (fatty tuna belly) is available at Jinbeh seasonally and based on what our seafood suppliers bring in that week. It is not a fixed daily menu item because true bluefin or yellowfin toro is expensive, sourced in limited quantity, and turns over quickly. When toro is available, you will often find it listed as a sushi bar special or on the daily specials card. Ask your sushi chef directly, they will know what came in that morning and whether toro (otoro, chutoro) is on the cut board. If you are planning a special occasion and specifically want toro, call ahead a day or two and we can try to reserve a portion from the next delivery.
questions.expandedContent: Toro is the prized fatty cut of tuna belly, prized for its marbling and melt-in-mouth texture. Otoro (the fattiest cut) is the most expensive and rarest; chutoro (medium-fatty) is more common. Toro pricing fluctuates significantly week-to-week based on tuna market prices, so we typically price it as market or daily special rather than a fixed menu item. If toro matters for your visit, call Frisco at (214) 619-1200 or Lewisville at (214) 488-2224 a day or two before to check availability. Pair toro with a clean junmai daiginjo sake or a glass of cold Japanese beer, the fatty richness pairs beautifully with crisp, clean drinks.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have Toro? | Fatty Tuna Belly at Our Sushi Bar
questions.metaDescription: Toro is available at Jinbeh seasonally based on tuna deliveries. Call ahead to reserve. Premium fatty tuna belly at our Frisco and Lewisville sushi bars.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have ramen?
questions.answer: Jinbeh is not currently serving ramen. Ramen was on the menu for many years and was popular with regular guests, but it has been removed from the current menu. For ramen lovers, Jinbeh recommends checking back later as menu items rotate over time. In the meantime, Jinbeh's current menu focuses on hibachi (teppanyaki grilled steak, chicken, shrimp, lobster, scallops, salmon, and vegetable-tofu entrees) and the full sushi bar (specialty rolls, sashimi, nigiri, and Chirashi bowls). Japanese onion soup is included with every hibachi entree, and other warm starter options include gyoza, tempura, and miso-based dishes. For the most current menu, call Frisco at (214) 619-1200 or Lewisville at (214) 488-2224.
questions.expandedContent: Menu changes at Jinbeh are made deliberately. The kitchen prioritizes quality and consistency on a smaller set of dishes rather than maintaining a wide menu where every item suffers. Ramen done right is a labor-intensive dish, and the family ownership made the call to focus the kitchen on hibachi and sushi instead. The decision is reviewed periodically, and ramen may return in the future. If ramen returns, it will be announced through the Jinbeh newsletter, social channels, and menu updates on the website.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have Ramen? | Not on the Current Menu
questions.metaDescription: Jinbeh used to serve ramen and it was popular, but it is not on the current menu. Current focus is hibachi and sushi at both Frisco and Lewisville locations.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have sake?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh has a curated sake list at both Frisco and Lewisville locations, including junmai, junmai ginjo, junmai daiginjo, nigori (unfiltered), and sparkling sake. We serve sake hot, cold, or chilled depending on the style, your server can recommend based on whether you are eating hibachi, sushi, or sashimi. Our happy hour Monday through Friday from 5 to 6:30 pm includes $5 sake by the glass, which is one of the best sake happy hour deals in Frisco or Lewisville. Sake by the bottle is available for larger groups or guests who want to share. The full bar also offers Japanese whisky, beer (Sapporo, Asahi, Kirin), wine, and cocktails.
questions.expandedContent: Sake pairing is where Japanese dining gets interesting. Crisp, dry junmai works with hibachi and grilled proteins. Junmai daiginjo (premium, polished rice) pairs beautifully with toro, sashimi, and delicate sushi. Nigori (unfiltered, slightly sweet, milky) is a crowd favorite for dessert or with spicier rolls. Sparkling sake is festive and great for celebrations. If you are new to sake, ask for a flight or order a glass during happy hour to taste before committing to a bottle. Our team can pour cold or warm depending on the bottle and your preference. Sake also makes a great gift, ask about taking a bottle home if Texas regulations allow at the time of your visit.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have Sake? | Curated Sake List & $5 Happy Hour
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh has a curated sake list with junmai, ginjo, daiginjo, nigori, and sparkling sake. $5 sake during happy hour Mon-Fri 5-6:30pm.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have Japanese whisky?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh stocks Japanese whisky at both Frisco and Lewisville full bars, including Suntory Toki, Hibiki, Yamazaki, Hakushu, and Nikka selections depending on availability. Japanese whisky has become difficult to source in recent years due to global demand outpacing Japan's production capacity, so specific labels rotate based on what we can get from distributors. Our bar also serves classic cocktails featuring Japanese whisky like the Toki highball (whisky and soda), Old Fashioned variations, and seasonal specials. If a specific bottle matters for your visit, call ahead to confirm what is on the back bar that week. Pair Japanese whisky with hibachi steak, grilled scallops, or fatty tuna for the best food pairings.
questions.expandedContent: Japanese whisky pricing has shifted significantly over the past decade as the category has gained global popularity. Hibiki and Yamazaki Limited Editions have become collector items; even standard Suntory Toki has occasional supply gaps. Jinbeh tries to keep a baseline Japanese whisky selection in stock for guests who want it. The Toki highball is the gateway drink, Japanese whisky over a tall ice cube with sparkling water and a citrus twist. Crisp, clean, and food-friendly. For sipping, ask the bartender what they have neat. If you are a Japanese whisky enthusiast, sit at the bar and have a conversation; our bartenders enjoy talking shop with guests who know the category.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have Japanese Whisky? | Suntory, Hibiki, Yamazaki
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh stocks Japanese whisky including Suntory Toki, Hibiki, Yamazaki, and Nikka based on availability. Pair with hibachi or sushi.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have a full bar?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh has a full bar at both Frisco and Lewisville locations. The bar serves sake (junmai through daiginjo and nigori), Japanese whisky, Japanese beer (Sapporo, Asahi, Kirin), domestic and craft beer, wine by the glass and bottle, and cocktails. Our happy hour runs Monday through Friday from 5pm to 6:30pm with $4 draft beer, $5 sake, and $6 wine, drinks only, dine-in only at both locations. The bar is a great spot for solo guests, couples, or anyone waiting for a hibachi table to open up. Cocktail favorites include the Toki highball, sake martini, lychee martini, and seasonal specials developed by our bartenders.
questions.expandedContent: Hibachi restaurants vary widely on bar programs, some are dry, some are wine-and-beer only, and some have full programs. Jinbeh has had a full bar for decades and treats it as an integral part of the experience. Sit at the bar before dinner to start with a sake or whisky flight, or stay at the bar all night for sushi and drinks. The bar is also where happy hour happens Monday through Friday 5-6:30 pm; the $4/$5/$6 deals on draft, sake, and wine make it one of the best happy hour values in Frisco or Lewisville. We do not currently offer happy hour food specials, happy hour is drinks only, but the full dinner menu is available at the bar.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have a Full Bar? | Sake, Whisky, Beer, Cocktails
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh has a full bar at Frisco and Lewisville with sake, Japanese whisky, beer, wine, and cocktails. Happy hour Mon-Fri 5-6:30pm: $4/$5/$6.

questions.question: What are Jinbeh's hours of operation?
questions.answer: Jinbeh is open daily for lunch and dinner. Lunch hours are Monday through Friday 11am to 2pm and Saturday through Sunday 11:30am to 2:30pm at both Frisco and Lewisville locations. Dinner hours are Sunday through Thursday 5pm to 9pm and Friday through Saturday 5pm to 10pm. We are typically closed for a few hours between lunch and dinner service. Happy hour runs Monday through Friday from 5pm to 6:30pm with $4 draft beer, $5 sake, and $6 wine. Hours may vary on major holidays, check our website or call Frisco at (214) 619-1200 or Lewisville at (214) 488-2224 to confirm before driving over.
questions.expandedContent: We are open seven days a week. The midday closure between roughly 2:30 pm and 5 pm gives the kitchen time to reset for dinner service and the chefs time to prep proteins, fish, and sauces. If you are looking for a late-afternoon meal, plan around dinner opening at 5 pm. Friday and Saturday nights are the busiest service windows and reservations are strongly recommended. Sunday dinner is often quieter and a good option for guests who want a hibachi experience without the weekend wait. Holiday hours can shift, we typically post updated hours on our website and Google Business Profile in advance.
questions.metaTitle: Jinbeh Hours of Operation | Lunch & Dinner in Frisco & Lewisville
questions.metaDescription: Jinbeh hours: Lunch Mon-Fri 11am-2pm, Sat-Sun 11:30am-2:30pm. Dinner Sun-Thu 5pm-9pm, Fri-Sat 5pm-10pm. Happy hour Mon-Fri 5-6:30pm.

questions.question: What are Jinbeh's lunch hours?
questions.answer: Jinbeh lunch hours are Monday through Friday from 11am to 2pm and Saturday through Sunday from 11:30am to 2:30pm at both Frisco and Lewisville locations. Lunch features a full lunch menu including hibachi, sushi, ramen, donburi, bento boxes, and our signature Hibachi-for-Two special ($35 total for two hibachi entrées Monday through Friday). Lunch reservations are accepted via OpenTable but often unnecessary on weekdays, walk-ins are usually seated quickly. Friday lunch and weekend brunch hours can run busier. The kitchen typically closes between lunch service (around 2:30pm) and dinner service opening at 5pm, so plan accordingly.
questions.expandedContent: Weekday lunch at Jinbeh is one of the best lunch values in DFW, especially the $35 Hibachi-for-Two deal. It is popular with date lunches, business meetings, mom groups, and anyone who wants a hibachi experience without dinner pricing. Lunch portions are sized for daytime appetite, substantial but not as heavy as full dinner portions. Saturday and Sunday lunch hours start at 11:30am because we use the extra prep time for weekend dinner volume. If you are coming during weekend lunch, expect a slightly busier dining room than weekday lunches. Reservations recommended for groups of four or more on weekends.
questions.metaTitle: Jinbeh Lunch Hours | Weekday 11am-2pm in Frisco & Lewisville
questions.metaDescription: Jinbeh lunch hours: Mon-Fri 11am-2pm, Sat-Sun 11:30am-2:30pm. Full lunch menu including Hibachi-for-Two for $35. Both DFW locations.

questions.question: Is Jinbeh open on Sunday?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh is open on Sundays at both Frisco and Lewisville locations. Sunday hours are: lunch 11:30am to 2:30pm and dinner 5pm to 9pm. Sunday is often quieter than Friday and Saturday nights, which makes it a good option for hibachi groups who want a more relaxed pace, families with young kids, or anyone hoping to avoid the weekend rush. Sunday dinner reservations are easier to get than peak weekend nights. The full menu including hibachi, sushi, ramen, and bar service is available all Sunday. Happy hour does not run on Sundays, happy hour is Monday through Friday 5pm to 6:30pm only.
questions.expandedContent: Sunday is a good 'shoulder' service day for guests who want a Friday-night experience without Friday-night wait times. Sunday brunch hours overlap with the lunch menu, so all the standard hibachi, sushi, ramen, and donburi options are available. Many families come on Sunday afternoon between sports practices and church activities. If you have a large group (8+) for Sunday dinner, mention it when you book on OpenTable, Sunday dinner staffing is slightly lighter and we want to be sure we have the right hibachi grill open for your party. Walk-ins on Sunday are typically seated quickly, but reservations still guarantee your time slot.
questions.metaTitle: Is Jinbeh Open on Sunday? | Sunday Hours in Frisco & Lewisville
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh is open Sundays. Lunch 11:30am-2:30pm, dinner 5pm-9pm. Often quieter than weekends; great for families and large groups.

questions.question: Is Jinbeh open on holidays?
questions.answer: Jinbeh's holiday hours vary by holiday and by location. We are typically open for Mother's Day, Father's Day, Valentine's Day, New Year's Eve, and most other holidays, these are some of our busiest service days and reservations are strongly recommended weeks in advance. We are typically closed on Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day. New Year's Day and Easter hours vary year to year. Always confirm holiday hours by calling Frisco at (214) 619-1200 or Lewisville at (214) 488-2224 or checking our Google Business Profile before driving over. Holiday reservations on OpenTable open earlier than usual, book at least 2 to 3 weeks in advance for major dining holidays.
questions.expandedContent: Mother's Day, Valentine's Day, and New Year's Eve are typically our highest-volume service days of the year. If those occasions matter to you, do not wait until the week of to book, we fill up. Father's Day and Easter Sunday are also popular for family hibachi. We are closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day to give our team time with their families; many of our chefs and servers have been with us for years, and time off matters. New Year's Eve typically runs full dinner service with extended hours; New Year's Day hours vary. Check our website, OpenTable, or call directly to confirm specific holiday plans.
questions.metaTitle: Is Jinbeh Open on Holidays? | Mother's Day, Valentine's, New Year's Eve
questions.metaDescription: Jinbeh is open most holidays including Mother's Day, Valentine's Day, and New Year's Eve. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas. Book 2-3 weeks ahead.

questions.question: How do I make a reservation at Jinbeh?
questions.answer: Reservations at Jinbeh can be made online through OpenTable (linked from our website) or by phone, Frisco at (214) 619-1200 and Lewisville at (214) 488-2224. OpenTable is the fastest option and shows real-time availability for both locations. Reservations are strongly recommended for dinner, Friday and Saturday nights, holidays, and large groups (6 or more). Walk-ins are welcome based on availability but may involve a wait during peak hours. For private dining, hibachi parties of 10+, or catering, call the location directly to speak with our events team. There is no fee to make a reservation and standard cancellation courtesy applies, please cancel as early as possible if plans change.
questions.expandedContent: OpenTable handles the vast majority of our reservations and lets you choose hibachi table seating, sushi bar, or a regular dining table at booking. Hibachi tables are seated communally, your party plus other parties to fill the grill, unless you book a private hibachi experience (typically 8+ guests). If you have a specific seating preference (booth, sushi bar, away from the door), add it as a note in the OpenTable booking or mention it when calling. For large parties, special occasions, and dietary needs, calling is usually the better path because you can discuss specifics with the host. Confirmation texts/emails arrive immediately after booking; we send reminders the day before.
questions.metaTitle: How Do I Make a Jinbeh Reservation? | OpenTable & Phone Booking
questions.metaDescription: Reserve at Jinbeh through OpenTable or call Frisco (214) 619-1200 / Lewisville (214) 488-2224. Walk-ins welcome based on availability.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh accept walk-ins?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh welcomes walk-ins at both Frisco and Lewisville locations based on availability. Walk-ins are typically seated quickly for lunch, weeknight dinners (Sunday through Thursday), and the sushi bar. Friday and Saturday nights, holidays, and large groups (6+) are more likely to face waits, reservations are strongly recommended for those times. If you walk in and there is a wait, the host will text you when your table is ready, so you are free to grab a drink at the bar (which itself often has open seats) or wait outside. Hibachi tables are seated communally, your walk-in group may share a grill with another party unless you wait for a full table.
questions.expandedContent: Walk-in volume is highest Friday 6-8pm and Saturday 6-9pm at both locations. If you have flexibility on timing, arriving at 5pm or after 8:30 pm during weekends gives the best chance of immediate seating. Lunch walk-ins are almost always quick. For groups of 6+, calling 30 minutes ahead even without a formal reservation lets us know you are coming and helps with table planning. The sushi bar is the best fallback for walk-ins on busy nights, sushi bar seats turn over faster than hibachi tables and you can get the full menu (including hibachi if you want) at the bar. If a wait is too long, ask the host about your other location's availability that night.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Accept Walk-Ins? | Yes, Based on Availability
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh accepts walk-ins at both Frisco and Lewisville. Reservations recommended for Friday/Saturday and large groups. Sushi bar is fastest seating.

questions.question: Is there parking at Jinbeh?
questions.answer: Yes, both Jinbeh locations have ample free parking. The Frisco location at 2693 Preston Road, Suite 1040 is in a shopping center near Stonebriar Centre with a large parking lot shared with other businesses in the plaza, parking is typically easy even on busy Friday and Saturday nights. The Lewisville location at 2440 S Stemmons Freeway is in a strip mall with dedicated parking right in front of the restaurant. Both locations are accessible without parallel parking or valet. ADA-accessible parking spaces are available at both. No parking fees apply. Plan to arrive 10 minutes before your reservation to give yourself time to park and walk in unhurried.
questions.expandedContent: Parking is rarely the issue at either Jinbeh location, both are in suburban-style shopping plazas built around generous parking ratios. Frisco's shopping center occasionally fills during peak shopping seasons (December, back-to-school weekends), but you can almost always find a spot within a short walk. Lewisville is even easier; the strip mall lot has spaces directly in front of the restaurant. Neither location offers valet, but both are walking-friendly from your car to the front door. If you are dropping off elderly or mobility-limited guests, you can use the curbside zone in front of the entrance at either location to drop off before parking. ADA-accessible spaces are clearly marked and located near the entrance.
questions.metaTitle: Is There Parking at Jinbeh? | Free Parking at Both DFW Locations
questions.metaDescription: Yes, both Jinbeh locations have ample free parking. Frisco in a shopping center near Stonebriar; Lewisville in a strip mall on Stemmons Freeway.

questions.question: Is there a dress code at Jinbeh?
questions.answer: Jinbeh has a casual to smart-casual dress code, there is no formal requirement, but guests typically dress neatly. Jeans, slacks, sundresses, and casual dresses are all appropriate. We ask that guests avoid beachwear (swimsuits, no shirts) and heavily soiled athletic wear out of consideration for other diners. For special occasions like anniversaries or business dinners, you will see guests dressed up; for a family weeknight hibachi visit, jeans and a clean t-shirt are perfectly fine. Children are welcome in any age-appropriate attire. Both Frisco and Lewisville locations apply the same standard. When in doubt, smart-casual is always a safe choice.
questions.expandedContent: Jinbeh's dress code is intentionally relaxed because we want to be the kind of restaurant you can fit into a Tuesday night, a soccer-game evening, or a date night without overthinking the outfit. We have served generations of DFW families and the dress code has stayed consistent across that time. If you are coming from work, business attire is welcome and common. If you are coming from a casual day, change clothes if you want but it is not required. Special occasions tend to bring out the dressier outfits, Valentine's Day, Mother's Day, anniversaries, birthdays, and you will see the room reflect that. Kids in soccer uniforms or birthday party clothes are always welcome.
questions.metaTitle: Is There a Dress Code at Jinbeh? | Casual to Smart-Casual
questions.metaDescription: Jinbeh dress code is casual to smart-casual. Jeans, slacks, dresses all welcome. No beachwear. Smart-casual works for any occasion.

questions.question: How long is the wait at Jinbeh?
questions.answer: Wait times at Jinbeh vary significantly by time and day. With a reservation, you should be seated within 10 minutes of your booked time. For walk-ins: weekday lunch and Sunday-Thursday dinner are typically immediate or under 15 minutes; Friday and Saturday 6pm-9pm walk-ins can wait 30 to 60 minutes for a hibachi table; the sushi bar usually has shorter waits than hibachi. A typical hibachi dinner runs 60 to 75 minutes from seating to check, and tables turn after that. If you are walk-in only on a weekend night, arriving at 5pm (right at open) or after 8:30 pm minimizes the wait. The host can text you when your table is ready.
questions.expandedContent: Hibachi tables seat groups of 6 to 10 communally, your party plus other parties fill the grill, so the wait can depend on how easily we can pair your group size with other parties waiting. A 2-top waiting for hibachi often waits longer than a 4-top because we need to find compatible partners. If you want a private hibachi table, the wait is longer and you may need to reserve. The sushi bar and dining tables (non-hibachi) have shorter waits. Reservations through OpenTable solve almost all wait issues, they take less than a minute to book and guarantee your seating window. Weekend dinner reservations 1-2 weeks out are usually still available.
questions.metaTitle: How Long Is the Wait at Jinbeh? | Wait Times & How to Avoid Them
questions.metaDescription: Jinbeh wait times: typically 10 min with a reservation. Walk-ins 0-60 min depending on time and day. Reserve via OpenTable to skip the wait.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have happy hour?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh has happy hour at both Frisco and Lewisville locations Monday through Friday from 5pm to 6:30pm. Happy hour pricing: $4 draft beer, $5 sake (by the glass), and $6 wine. Happy hour is drinks only, there are no discounted food specials during happy hour, and it is dine-in only at the bar or any table. The full dinner menu is available the entire time, including hibachi, sushi, and small plates at regular pricing. Happy hour is one of the best sake happy hour deals in Frisco or Lewisville, and the early dinner window is also a great time to grab a hibachi seat without weekend wait times. No reservation needed for happy hour drinks.
questions.expandedContent: Happy hour at Jinbeh started as a way to give early-evening guests a reason to come in during the 5pm-6:30pm shoulder window before the dinner rush. The $4/$5/$6 pricing on draft, sake, and wine is competitive with most Frisco and Lewisville bars and significantly cheaper than typical sake pricing at sit-down sushi restaurants. Sake by the glass during happy hour is a great way to taste different styles before committing to a bottle, junmai, ginjo, nigori, sparkling rotations available. Happy hour pairs well with sushi appetizers, edamame, gyoza, or just a low-key catch-up with a friend before heading to dinner. Holidays may shift happy hour timing; check ahead if you are coming on a holiday.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have Happy Hour? | Mon-Fri 5-6:30pm | $4 Draft, $5 Sake
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh happy hour Mon-Fri 5-6:30pm. $4 draft beer, $5 sake, $6 wine. Both Frisco and Lewisville locations. Drinks only, dine-in.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh offer catering?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh offers catering for corporate events, weddings, birthday parties, graduations, and special occasions across the Dallas-Fort Worth area. Catering options include sushi platters (party trays of nigiri, sashimi, and rolls), Japanese entrée trays, hibachi-style buffet setups, bento boxes, and customizable menus built around your guest count and budget. We can deliver to your office, home, or event venue, or arrange pickup from either the Frisco or Lewisville location. Catering pricing scales with menu choices, guest count, and service style. Call Frisco at (214) 619-1200 or Lewisville at (214) 488-2224 to speak with our catering team, most events benefit from 1 to 2 weeks of lead time.
questions.expandedContent: Catering at Jinbeh draws on the same recipes and standards as our dine-in service: fresh fish, real teppanyaki technique, and the signature mustard sauce that DFW guests know us for. Sushi platters are our most popular catering item, they travel well, look beautiful on a buffet, and accommodate a wide range of dietary preferences with vegetarian rolls in the mix. For larger events, we can build custom menus combining sushi, cooked entrées, sides, and desserts. Hibachi-style live cooking at events is possible with advance planning and the right venue (we need ventilation and a compatible cooking surface). Tell us your headcount, date, venue, and any dietary restrictions when you call so we can quote accurately.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Offer Catering? | DFW Japanese Catering & Sushi Platters
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh caters corporate events, weddings, and parties across DFW. Sushi platters, hibachi-style setups, bento boxes. Call Frisco or Lewisville.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh do on-site hibachi catering?
questions.answer: Jinbeh does not currently offer on-site hibachi performances at off-property events, meaning a chef does not travel to your home, office, or venue to perform the tableside hibachi show. However, Jinbeh does offer hibachi catering delivery: the kitchen prepares hibachi-style entrees (steak, chicken, shrimp, salmon, vegetables, fried rice, signature sauces) and delivers them hot to your event. This delivers the flavor and food quality of the Jinbeh hibachi experience to your group without the tableside performance. For the full tableside hibachi show including the onion volcano and knife tricks, the experience is available in-restaurant at both Frisco and Lewisville locations, where private hibachi rooms can accommodate parties of 8 to 30 or more.
questions.expandedContent: Catering delivery options include sushi platters (specialty rolls, sashimi, nigiri), hibachi-style hot entrees in catering trays or individual portions, bento boxes for office lunches, and full a la carte spreads for weddings, corporate events, and private parties. For groups that want the tableside hibachi show, the best path is to host the event at one of the Jinbeh restaurants in a private dining room. Private hibachi rooms can accommodate parties of 8 to 30 or more, and the events team can coordinate custom menus, beverage packages, and special occasion acknowledgments. questions.expandedContent: Private dining at Jinbeh combines the hibachi experience with the privacy and customization most groups want for a special occasion. questions.answer: Absolutely, Jinbeh is one of the most popular birthday party destinations in Frisco and Lewisville. questions.metaDescription: Jinbeh is a top DFW birthday party destination, hibachi show, onion volcano, private dining for groups. Frisco and Lewisville locations.

questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh is well-suited for corporate events, team dinners, client entertainment, executive retreats, holiday parties, and recruiting dinners. questions.metaDescription: Jinbeh hosts corporate events for 8-60+ guests at Frisco and Lewisville. Team dinners, client entertainment, holiday parties. Invoicing available.

questions.question: Is Jinbeh good for special occasions?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh has been a go-to special occasion destination in DFW since 1988. questions.expandedContent: Special occasions deserve a venue that knows how to deliver them. Jinbeh's long tenure means our team has handled thousands of celebrations, we know what to do without needing detailed instructions. If it is a birthday, the chef plays it up. For milestone birthdays and anniversaries, ask about private dining; for smaller occasions, a regular hibachi table works perfectly. questions.question: How far in advance should I book catering or private dining?
questions.answer: Most catering and private dining bookings at Jinbeh benefit from 1 to 4 weeks of lead time. For smaller catering orders (sushi platters, bento boxes for 10-30 guests), 3 to 7 days is often sufficient. For private dining in our Frisco or Lewisville dining rooms with custom menus, plan 2 to 4 weeks ahead. For peak dates, Mother's Day, Valentine's, graduation season (May/June), and December holiday parties, book 4 to 8 weeks out. For full restaurant buyouts or weddings, 8 to 12 weeks is realistic. Last-minute requests are sometimes accommodated based on staffing and kitchen capacity. Call early; we can almost always get back to you within a business day with options.
questions.expandedContent: Lead time matters because the kitchen and front-of-house need to plan: protein orders, fish deliveries, staff scheduling, and table arrangement all have to align. Sushi platters require a day or two of notice for the sushi chefs to order the right quantity of fish; custom menus take longer to design and quote. Peak season (graduation, holidays, Mother's Day) is when lead times stretch the most because we are protecting capacity for regular reservations. If you have a specific date in mind, call as soon as you do; we can hold a tentative date while you finalize headcount. For weddings, rehearsal dinners, and 50+ guest events, work with us at least 2 months ahead.
questions.metaTitle: How Far in Advance to Book Jinbeh Catering? | Lead Time Guide
questions.metaDescription: Book Jinbeh catering 1-4 weeks ahead, private dining 2-4 weeks, weddings 8-12 weeks. Peak dates (May, December, holidays) book earlier.

questions.question: Is Jinbeh good for rehearsal dinners or weddings?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh hosts rehearsal dinners and wedding-related events at both Frisco and Lewisville locations. Rehearsal dinners (typically 15-40 guests) work especially well in our private dining areas where the hibachi format creates immediate energy and conversation among families meeting for the first time. Book 8 to 12 weeks ahead for wedding-related events, especially in peak wedding season (April-October).
questions.expandedContent: Rehearsal dinners are one of our favorite events because the hibachi format does the work of breaking the ice between two families. By the time the chef finishes the onion volcano, parents-in-law are laughing and the wedding-week tension has dropped. We can build a set menu, accommodate dietary restrictions across the group, and coordinate timing with toasts and slideshows. For wedding catering off-site, our most popular packages are sushi platter spreads (visually stunning, dietary-flexible) and Japanese buffet trays. Bridal showers often book the sushi bar area for a more intimate feel. Discuss your specific needs with our events team, we have done dozens of wedding-related events over the years.

questions.metaDescription: Jinbeh hosts rehearsal dinners (15-40 guests) and caters weddings off-site. Sushi platters, hibachi buffets, custom Japanese menus. Book 8-12 weeks ahead.

questions.question: Is there a minimum group size for a hibachi table?
questions.answer: There is no strict minimum group size to sit at a hibachi table at Jinbeh, even solo diners and 2-tops can request hibachi seating. However, hibachi tables seat 6 to 10 guests communally around a single grill, so smaller parties (1-4 guests) are typically seated with other parties to fill the table. If you want a private hibachi table without sharing the grill, you generally need 8 to 10 guests to book the full table privately. Smaller groups who do not want to share can choose a dining table or sushi bar instead. Mention your preference (share or private) when you book on OpenTable or call.
questions.expandedContent: Communal hibachi seating is part of what makes the experience special, strangers become friends over a 75-minute meal and a shared chef performance. For many guests it is a feature. But some occasions (a quiet anniversary, a sensitive business meeting, a kids' birthday with strict guest list) work better with a private table. The math is simple: a single hibachi grill costs the same to operate whether 4 people or 10 are seated, so we need enough revenue at the table to justify dedicating the grill privately. 8 to 10 guests typically does it; smaller groups can buy out a table for an additional charge in some cases. Ask when you book.
questions.metaTitle: Hibachi Group Minimum at Jinbeh | Communal & Private Tables
questions.metaDescription: No minimum group size for hibachi at Jinbeh, small parties share tables. Private hibachi tables typically require 8-10 guests. Book on OpenTable.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have gluten-free options?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh has gluten-free options at both Frisco and Lewisville locations. Hibachi proteins (chicken, steak, shrimp, scallops, salmon, filet mignon) can be cooked gluten-free using gluten-free tamari instead of regular soy sauce, just inform your server and hibachi chef before the chef starts cooking. Sushi options like sashimi, nigiri, and many basic rolls can be made gluten-free as long as you skip soy sauce or request gluten-free tamari. Fried rice contains soy sauce and is not gluten-free as standard; we can substitute steamed white rice. Tempura, teriyaki, and most sauces contain wheat. Always tell us about gluten sensitivity or celiac at the beginning of the meal so we can take cross-contamination precautions on the grill.
questions.expandedContent: Celiac-level gluten sensitivity requires extra care because hibachi grills are shared surfaces. If you have celiac disease (not just gluten sensitivity), tell your server when you sit down, we can clean the grill surface, use a separate spatula, and cook your protein in a dedicated area. Gluten-free tamari is available on request as a soy sauce substitute. Mustard sauce and ginger sauce are typically gluten-free; check current ingredient lists with your server. Yum yum sauce may contain trace gluten depending on the soy sauce used. Our sushi chefs can build gluten-free rolls with no tempura, no fried fillings, and no flavored cream cheese, ask for the simplest preparations.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have Gluten-Free Options? | GF Hibachi & Sushi
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh has gluten-free options including hibachi proteins with gluten-free tamari, sashimi, and modified sushi rolls. Tell us about celiac when you arrive.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have vegetarian options?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh has vegetarian options at both Frisco and Lewisville locations. The vegetarian hibachi entrée includes hibachi vegetables (zucchini, onion, mushroom, bell pepper) and tofu cooked on the grill alongside fried rice. The full hibachi experience, chef performance, onion volcano, sauces, is available vegetarian. Sushi vegetarian options include cucumber rolls, avocado rolls, vegetable rolls, sweet potato tempura rolls, and inari (tofu skin). Sides like edamame, miso soup, seaweed salad, vegetable tempura, and gyoza (vegetable version) round out the vegetarian menu. Inform your server of vegetarian preferences so they can flag sauces and stocks that may contain fish (like bonito-based dashi in miso soup).
questions.expandedContent: Hibachi is naturally accommodating to vegetarians because the chef cooks each protein separately on the grill. Vegetable hibachi gets the same fried rice, vegetables, soup, salad, and sauces as a chicken or steak hibachi, minus the meat. Tofu can be added for protein. If you are dining with non-vegetarians at the same hibachi table, no problem: the chef simply cooks vegetable portions on one side of the grill. For strict vegetarians who avoid fish-derived ingredients, note that traditional miso soup uses dashi (bonito-based stock); ask for vegetable broth substitution if available. Sushi rice itself is typically vegetarian. Sauces vary, yum yum and mustard sauce are typically vegetarian; check with your server.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have Vegetarian Options? | Veggie Hibachi & Sushi
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh has vegetarian hibachi with tofu, vegetable sushi rolls, edamame, miso soup, and tempura. Both Frisco and Lewisville locations.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have vegan options?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh has vegan options at both locations. Vegan hibachi is available with vegetables and tofu, no butter or eggs, tell your server and chef that you are vegan so they can adjust (most hibachi uses butter on the grill and egg in the fried rice). Steamed white rice or noodles can be substituted. Vegan sushi options include cucumber rolls, avocado rolls, sweet potato tempura rolls (skip the eel sauce), and custom vegetable rolls. Edamame, seaweed salad (check dressing), and steamed rice are vegan. Avoid yum yum sauce (contains mayo), mustard sauce (contains cream), and miso soup (often uses fish-based dashi). Stick to soy sauce, ginger sauce, and simple preparations. Vegan dining works with advance notice and clear communication.
questions.expandedContent: Vegan dining at a hibachi restaurant requires more communication than vegetarian dining because of the butter and egg defaults in traditional hibachi cooking. Tell the host you are vegan when you book, remind your server when seated, and remind the chef when they arrive at the grill. The vegan-friendly hibachi setup: oil instead of butter, no egg in the fried rice (or substitute steamed white rice), vegetables and tofu, soy sauce and ginger sauce. For sushi, the safest vegan rolls are simple ones, cucumber, avocado, vegetable, sweet potato. Most specialty rolls contain mayo, cream cheese, or fish-based sauces. Inari (sweet tofu pouches) is vegan and a tasty option. Ask the sushi chef to build a custom vegan platter.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have Vegan Options? | Vegan Hibachi & Sushi in DFW
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh has vegan hibachi (no butter, no egg) with tofu and vegetables, plus vegan sushi options. Communicate clearly when you arrive.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh accommodate food allergies?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh takes food allergies seriously at both Frisco and Lewisville locations and accommodates common allergies daily, including gluten, dairy, peanut, tree nut, shellfish, soy, sesame, and egg allergies. Tell your server about any allergy as soon as you arrive, and remind your hibachi chef when they reach your table. For severe allergies (anaphylactic-level), we can clean grill surfaces, use separate utensils, and cook your portion in a dedicated area to reduce cross-contamination. Our kitchen tracks common allergen ingredients across the menu and can identify safe options. Some menu items inherently contain allergens (shellfish in many sushi rolls, soy in most sauces, gluten in tempura) and may not be modifiable, your server will guide you.
questions.expandedContent: Cross-contamination is the biggest risk at any restaurant, especially on a hibachi grill where many proteins are cooked in sequence on the same surface. Our chefs follow standard protocols: wipe down the grill, use clean spatulas, and isolate the allergen-sensitive portion when needed. For peanut and tree nut allergies, Jinbeh does not feature peanuts prominently, we are not a Thai or Chinese kitchen, but trace cross-contact is possible from shared kitchen spaces. For severe nut allergies, communicate this clearly and we will check ingredient lists. Shellfish allergy is more challenging because shrimp is cooked on the same grill regularly; we can mitigate but not eliminate cross-contact. Always disclose severity (sensitivity vs anaphylaxis) so we can match precaution level.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Accommodate Food Allergies? | Allergy-Aware Dining
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh accommodates gluten, dairy, nut, shellfish, soy, and egg allergies. Communicate at arrival; chefs follow cross-contamination protocols.

questions.question: Is sushi at Jinbeh safe during pregnancy?
questions.answer: Most medical guidance recommends pregnant women avoid raw fish sushi due to risks of foodborne illness and mercury exposure. Jinbeh sources high-quality sushi-grade fish following industry-standard handling protocols, but no restaurant can guarantee zero risk with raw fish. Cooked sushi options at Jinbeh are pregnancy-safe and plentiful: shrimp tempura rolls, California rolls (cooked crab), eel (unagi) rolls, vegetable rolls, sweet potato tempura rolls, and any roll with all cooked ingredients. Hibachi is also a fully cooked, pregnancy-safe option, protein cooked to high temperature on the grill. If you are pregnant, talk with your doctor about your specific guidelines and stick to cooked menu items when dining out. Our servers can help identify cooked-only options.
questions.expandedContent: The standard medical concern with sushi during pregnancy is twofold: parasitic/bacterial risk from raw fish, and mercury content from larger predatory fish like bluefin tuna. Cooked fish, vegetable, and grain-based sushi is widely considered safe. At Jinbeh, your pregnancy-safe sushi options include: California roll (imitation crab is cooked), Boston roll (cooked shrimp), shrimp tempura roll, dynamite roll (cooked), unagi roll (cooked eel), sweet potato tempura roll, cucumber roll, avocado roll, vegetable roll, and inari. Hibachi is fully safe, chicken, steak, shrimp, scallops are all cooked to temperature. Skip raw fish sashimi, raw tuna or salmon nigiri, and rolls containing raw fish until after delivery. Always consult your own physician for personalized guidance.
questions.metaTitle: Is Jinbeh Sushi Safe During Pregnancy? | Cooked Sushi Options
questions.metaDescription: Pregnant guests can choose cooked sushi at Jinbeh, California, tempura, eel, and vegetable rolls. Hibachi is fully cooked and pregnancy-safe.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have a kids menu?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh has a kids menu at both Frisco and Lewisville locations. Kids hibachi entrées include scaled-down portions of chicken, shrimp, or steak with fried rice and vegetables, served with the same chef performance as the adult menu.
