Children love the hibachi experience, the chef's egg toss, knife tricks, and onion volcano are crowd-pleasers across all ages. High chairs and booster seats are available. For kids with picky palates, the chefs can omit vegetables, sauces, or adjust seasoning on request.
questions.expandedContent: Hibachi is one of the most family-friendly dining formats because the entertainment built into the meal keeps kids engaged through dinner. Our chefs are practiced with kids and adjust their show accordingly, bigger fire tricks for older kids, gentler tricks (like the egg toss) for younger ones. For very young kids (under 4) who might be startled by the flames, mention this when you book and we can seat your family at a regular dining table rather than the hibachi grill. The kids menu portions are sized so that most children finish without leftovers, but we are happy to box up anything that comes home. Birthday parties for kids are one of our most common booking types.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have a Kids Menu? | Family-Friendly Hibachi Menu
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh has a kids menu with hibachi chicken, shrimp, steak, fried rice, and sushi. Family-friendly with high chairs and chef performances for all ages.

questions.question: Is hibachi at Jinbeh healthy?
questions.answer: Hibachi at Jinbeh can be a healthy dining choice depending on what you order and how it is prepared. The cooking method itself, high-heat grilling on a flat iron surface, uses less oil than deep-frying or pan-saucing, and the proteins (chicken, shrimp, scallops, steak, salmon) come grilled without breading. Vegetables get the same treatment. The two main calorie drivers in a hibachi meal are fried rice (made with oil, butter, and egg) and the dipping sauces (especially yum yum sauce, which is mayo-based). For a lighter hibachi, ask for steamed white rice instead of fried rice, use ginger sauce instead of yum yum or mustard sauce, and skip the soup-and-salad upcharges.
questions.expandedContent: A typical hibachi chicken meal at Jinbeh runs roughly 700-1200 calories depending on rice choice and sauce usage. Steak and shrimp versions can range higher. For comparison, that is roughly equivalent to many sit-down restaurant entrées. To lower the calorie count: steamed rice instead of fried rice saves 200-300 calories; ginger sauce instead of yum yum or mustard saves 100-200 calories; skipping the butter on the grill (ask for oil only) saves another 100 calories. Vegetables and lean proteins (chicken, shrimp, scallops) are the leanest hibachi options. Sushi options vary widely, sashimi and nigiri are the leanest; tempura rolls and rolls with cream cheese or mayo are richest. Eat well, enjoy the show.
questions.metaTitle: Is Hibachi at Jinbeh Healthy? | Calorie & Nutrition Guide
questions.metaDescription: Hibachi at Jinbeh can be healthy, grilled proteins, vegetables. Save calories with steamed rice over fried rice and ginger sauce over yum yum.

questions.question: How many calories are in hibachi at Jinbeh?
questions.primaryKeyword: how many calories in jinbeh hibachi
questions.answer: A typical hibachi meal at Jinbeh ranges from approximately 700 to 1500 calories depending on protein, rice choice, and sauce usage. Hibachi chicken with fried rice and vegetables averages around 900-1100 calories with sauces; the same meal with steamed white rice and ginger sauce drops to about 700-800. Hibachi steak runs higher due to the cut and added butter, often 1100-1400 calories. Shrimp and scallop hibachi sits in the middle, around 800-1000. Lobster and filet mignon combinations can push above 1400. These are estimates, we do not publish exact nutritional information because portions and preparation vary by chef and order. Ask your server for guidance on lighter modifications.
questions.expandedContent: To put hibachi calories in context: a typical American sit-down restaurant entrée runs 1000-1500 calories, so hibachi is in the same range. The calorie drivers are the fried rice (oil, butter, egg), the butter used on the grill, and the dipping sauces (yum yum sauce is mayo-based and calorie-dense; mustard sauce is creamy; ginger sauce is the leanest). Onion soup and salad with ginger dressing add about 200-300 calories combined. If you are tracking calories carefully, the easiest moves: steamed rice instead of fried (saves 250+ cal), one sauce instead of three, vegetable upgrade with less butter, lean protein (chicken or shrimp) over steak. Our team will modify any hibachi order on request.
questions.metaTitle: How Many Calories in Hibachi at Jinbeh? | Hibachi Calorie Estimates
questions.metaDescription: Hibachi at Jinbeh ranges from 700-1500 calories depending on protein and rice. Lighten with steamed rice, ginger sauce, and lean proteins.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have low-sodium options?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh can accommodate low-sodium dietary needs at both Frisco and Lewisville locations with advance notice. Hibachi proteins (chicken, steak, shrimp, scallops) can be cooked without added soy sauce or salt, tell your server and chef when you arrive and they will use minimal seasoning on the grill. Steamed white rice has less sodium than fried rice. Sashimi and basic nigiri can be enjoyed with reduced or no soy sauce (low-sodium soy sauce is available on request at most times). Sauces vary: yum yum is moderate, mustard and ginger are moderate to higher. Miso soup and any teriyaki preparations are naturally higher in sodium. Communicate your needs at the start of the meal for best results.
questions.expandedContent: Japanese cooking generally relies on soy sauce, miso, and salt-cured ingredients, which means sodium content is something to manage actively rather than assume. The lowest-sodium hibachi configuration: grilled chicken or shrimp with vegetables, steamed white rice, no marinade, no soy sauce on the grill, and using lemon or a small amount of ginger sauce for flavor. Sushi lowest-sodium configuration: sashimi (just the fish) with no soy sauce, or low-sodium tamari on the side. Skip preparations advertised as teriyaki, miso, or katsu, these are higher sodium. For guests managing hypertension or kidney conditions, tell your server clearly and we will work with you. Chefs adjust readily for low-sodium guests with notice.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have Low-Sodium Options? | Low-Salt Hibachi & Sushi
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh accommodates low-sodium diets. Grilled proteins without soy or salt, steamed rice, sashimi with low-sodium tamari. Tell us at arrival.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh have tofu?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh serves tofu at both Frisco and Lewisville locations as part of the vegetarian and vegan hibachi entrées and as an option in soups and salads. Tofu hibachi includes firm tofu cooked on the grill alongside vegetables, fried rice, and the chef's tableside performance, it gets the same treatment as the meat-based hibachi entrées with the choice of mustard, ginger, or yum yum sauce. For vegan diners, request no butter on the grill and steamed rice instead of fried (which contains egg). Tofu also appears in some miso soup preparations and can be added to sushi rolls as inari (sweet tofu pouches) or in custom vegetable rolls. Confirm preparation details with your server based on dietary needs.
questions.expandedContent: Tofu hibachi is one of our most-popular vegetarian entrées because it scratches the hibachi itch, same show, same fried rice, same sauces, without meat. Firm tofu grills well and absorbs the flavors of the grill, garlic, and sauces. For vegan guests, the trick is asking for the cooking modifications (oil instead of butter, no egg in rice or skip fried rice) so the dish stays plant-based. Mixed groups work easily: one diner can order tofu hibachi while others have chicken or steak, all cooked simultaneously by the chef. Inari sushi (sweet, marinated tofu pouches filled with sushi rice) is another tofu-based option from the sushi side of the menu. Quick, vegan, and a nice palate-cleanser between rolls.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Have Tofu? | Tofu Hibachi & Vegan Options
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh serves tofu hibachi with grilled vegetables, fried rice, and the full chef performance. Also tofu in miso soup and inari sushi.

questions.question: Does Jinbeh do sushi takeout and delivery?
questions.answer: Yes, Jinbeh offers sushi takeout and delivery at both Frisco and Lewisville locations. Order takeout by calling Frisco at (214) 619-1200 or Lewisville at (214) 488-2224, or order through Grubhub or Uber Eats for delivery. Takeout sushi typically takes 15 to 30 minutes depending on how busy we are; call ahead to time your pickup. Sushi travels well, including nigiri, sashimi, classic rolls, and most specialty rolls. Hibachi is dine-in only, the rice, vegetables, and proteins do not translate to takeout containers. Non-hibachi cooked entrées like chicken teriyaki, tempura, and ramen are also available for takeout. Sushi platters for catering and parties can be ordered with advance notice.
questions.expandedContent: Sushi takeout is a great option for date nights at home, family movie nights, or sushi parties where you want to skip cooking but stay in. Order classics like California rolls, salmon nigiri, spicy tuna rolls, and rainbow rolls, they all hold up well in transit. More delicate items like uni or fatty toro are best eaten at the sushi bar. For party platters (12+ pieces), order at least a day ahead so the sushi chefs can plan fish quantities. Grubhub and Uber Eats handle delivery; both are tied to our menu in real time. You can also call us directly for pickup orders. If you have allergies or modifications, calling direct is better than ordering through the apps.
questions.metaTitle: Does Jinbeh Do Sushi Takeout? | Order Online or Call
questions.metaDescription: Yes, Jinbeh offers sushi takeout and delivery through Grubhub, Uber Eats, and direct call orders at both Frisco and Lewisville locations.

questions.question: What payment methods does Jinbeh accept?
questions.answer: Jinbeh accepts all major credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover), debit cards, and cash at both Frisco and Lewisville locations. We also accept digital wallet payments including Apple Pay and Google Pay at most points of sale. For large parties and corporate events, we can split checks across multiple cards or set up a single corporate invoice with advance arrangement. Gift cards purchased at Jinbeh are accepted at both locations interchangeably. For online takeout orders through Grubhub or Uber Eats, payment methods follow the platform's policies. Personal checks are not accepted for standard service. Gratuity may be added automatically for parties of 8 or more, confirm at the time of service.
questions.expandedContent: Payment is intentionally simple. Almost every standard payment method is accepted, and our point-of-sale system handles split checks for groups (within reason, please let your server know ahead of time if you need a 6-way split so we can prepare). questions.question: Do I tip the hibachi chef at Jinbeh?
questions.answer: Tipping the hibachi chef is appreciated but not required at Jinbeh, you are not obligated. Standard practice in DFW hibachi: tip your server 18-20% on the meal as usual, and separately offer the hibachi chef a tip (often $5 to $20 depending on group size and how much you enjoyed the performance) if they exceeded expectations. Some guests roll the chef tip into the server tip; others hand cash directly to the chef at the end of the show. There is no wrong way. The chef and the server are typically separate tip pools, so a separate tip for the chef goes to them directly. If the entire experience was outstanding, generous tipping on both is always appreciated.
questions.expandedContent: Tipping etiquette varies regionally and is often a source of confusion at hibachi restaurants. The reason the chef tip is conventional is that hibachi chefs perform a separate service from the server, the show, the cooking, the entertainment, that goes beyond what your standard server does. Many chefs build personal relationships with regular guests over years; tipping is one way to recognize that. For first-time hibachi guests at Jinbeh, $5-10 per couple to the chef is generous and well-received; for large parties, $20-30 to the chef is appropriate. None of this is required, and your meal will not change based on your tip. If you are unsure, ask your server for guidance.

questions.expandedContent: Different times suit different visit types. Date nights work well Tuesday through Thursday evenings, quieter dining room, easier reservations, and you avoid the weekend crowds. questions.question: What is the onion volcano at hibachi?
questions.answer: The onion volcano is the signature hibachi performance trick where the chef stacks sliced onion rings into a small tower on the grill, pours oil into the center, and lights it on fire, producing a tall flame that resembles an erupting volcano. It is the visual centerpiece of the hibachi show and arguably the most-photographed moment of any hibachi meal. At Jinbeh, the onion volcano happens early in the cooking sequence as a built-in 'show-starter' before the chef begins cooking proteins. Kids especially love it. The trick has been part of hibachi tradition at our restaurants since 1988. After the flame dies down, the cooked onions are spread on the grill and become part of the meal.
questions.expandedContent: The onion volcano is functionally useful in addition to being visually impressive, the flame quickly heats and slightly caramelizes the onion rings, releasing flavor that infuses the rest of the meal cooked on that grill surface. It also signals the start of the show to the table: when the volcano lights up, the meal is officially underway. Different hibachi chefs have different variations, some build taller towers, some add smoke effects, some incorporate the volcano into the egg toss or the timing of other tricks. Our long-tenured Jinbeh chefs each have their own style developed over years. Tell us if you are celebrating a birthday or special occasion; the chef often pulls out the bigger version of the volcano.

Happy Hour Mon-Fri 5-6:30 PM offers $4 draft, $5 sake, $6 wine.
questions.expandedContent: What you actually pay for: a serious sushi program (not the afterthought sushi some hibachi competitors serve), proteins that match the menu description (no swapped-cut allegations), fresh fish delivered regularly, and consistent quality from chefs who have been at Jinbeh for 10 to nearly 30 years. Reviews from competitors often mention dry rice, stingy portions, or imitation crab where the menu said real, none of which apply at Jinbeh. For a budget-conscious approach, the weekday lunch special, happy hour, and the kids menu keep the total well below $25 per person. For special occasions, the premium combination platters and a sake flight can push higher. Most guests find Jinbeh a strong value relative to corporate chains at the same price point.

Jinbeh's chefs have tenures of 10 years and more, and the Gracious Host hospitality philosophy means the performance is tailored to your table rather than scripted.
